title: Spend Round Trips, Not Calls
tagline: Batching is part of the tool signature, because a request in a prompt is one a model can stop honouring.

story.problem: A traced scout run spent 166 of its 220 seconds in the decision about the next call, and 27 seconds in the tools. The source did not attribute the remainder. The couple does not wait for the provider. The couple waits for the model's turn, and one turn occurs for each tool call that the model decides to make. Also, a tool-calling transcript sends every prior turn again. Thus each added round trip reads a transcript that grew since the last trip, and the bill counts a returned result again on every later model call. The scout instructions asked for batched searches before web_search could accept one. That made batching a request that the model could quietly ignore.
story.solution: Move batching into the tool signature: agent/tools/web_search.ts takes queries as an array with a cap of four, runs the queries through one Promise.all, and returns the results grouped by query. Both queries and query stay optional, so neither shape can cause a schema failure — a schema that cannot be satisfied kills a subagent session. An empty batch returns the status no_query and does not throw. filterSeen in agent/lib/search-budget.ts removes the URLs that the session has already seen. It applies across the whole batch, not per query, and it is bounded to the last 400. The scout's todo tool is disabled, because it spent two round trips on records that the search budget already bounds. The same batching rule applies one level up: the planner dispatches every scout in a single response.
story.outcome: One committed RunResult, runs/eve-boston-boho.json, shows five scouts that take 23, 15, 14, 15 and 12 steps against 6, 4, 4, 2 and 4 web_search calls — 20 search calls across 79 steps. The concurrent fan-out puts 335.8s of scout time inside a 114.0s run. The slowest scout takes 75.5s, and the planner is parked for 102,781ms of its own. No gate uses a latency figure: the wall clock is measured and published, never asserted. record_vendor stays unbatched by design, because a finding that does not survive a truncation is worse than a slow finding.

prerequisites: An eve install with declared subagents and defineState (^0.24.4)
TAVILY_API_KEY for live search and NEBIUS_API_KEY for the model — the command in the recipe needs neither
Recipe 05 (Governance): the per-session query counter this tool reserves against before it dials out
More than one traced run, if you want to know whether a change moved anything

quickstart.clone: git clone https://github.com/jaredwerba/vendor-scout.git && cd vendor-scout && npm install
quickstart.configure: Nothing to configure to read the committed run artifact. To regenerate it against the live deployment, put the KV credentials (KV_REST_API_URL and KV_REST_API_TOKEN) in .env.local and run npm run run:eve -- boston-boho; the model and search keys live on the deployment it drives.
